chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Yahya ibn Mihran from Abdullah ibn al-Hasan said:

I asked him about the Qaramil. He said, 'What is the Qaramil?' I said, 'Wool that women place on their heads.' He said, 'If it is wool, there is no harm; but if it is hair, there is no good in it, like the connected (hair extensions).'

key_terms.الْقَرَامِلُ: A type of head covering or ornament, specifically wool or hair.
key_terms.الْوَاصِلَةِ: The connected one (referring to hair extensions or attached hair).
key_terms.وَلَا خَيْرَ فِيهِ: There is no good in it (disliked or inferior).

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on women using hair-based head coverings or extensions in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between the permissibility of wool (*suf*) and the impermissibility of hair (*sha'r*) used in the 'Qaramil', a head ornament. The comparison to *al-Wasilah* (the hair-braider or one who adds hair) highlights the specific prohibition against using human hair for extension or attachment, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on material purity and the nature of the added element in adornment.
